claim: A bay charges a pack from 20 to 80 % in about 1.2 h
law: Charge = current x time: 0.6 x 10 Ah at the 5 A constant-current stage

claim: A pack charges from empty to full in about 2.3 h at 25 C
law: Constant current to 85 % (1.7 h), then a 0.6 h tapering constant-voltage stage (SWC-CAL-001)

claim: Four bays draw a peak of 1.25 kW from the grid
law: P = 4 x (54.6 V x 5 A / 0.90) plus 40 W of cabinet load; an upper bound, since one bay is always empty and the simulated day never runs more than 3 chargers at once
closed_by: DKH-CAL-001 s6 (1253 W; 3 chargers at once in the simulated day)

claim: Daily energy at 20 swaps: grid and solar in equal stored energy plus losses
law: Conservation of energy over a day (first law); the losses are computed independently as 10 % in the charger and 5 % in the cells (0.80 and 0.40 kWh), not by subtraction

claim: A 400 W panel gives about 1.38 kWh a day at the MPPT output (4.5 sun hours); 0.74 kWh of it reaches the packs
law: Rated power x peak sun hours x 0.8 derate x 0.96 MPPT efficiency

claim: At most 36 swaps a day from 3 resident packs released full (55 at the adopted 80 % release; 24 with one bay out of service)
law: Packs x hours in a day / hours to recharge a returned pack (15 to 100 %, 2.0 h)

claim: A swap takes 60 s or less for a familiar rider
law: Sum of the task steps: tap 3, unlock 1, open and place 8, close 2, confirm 2, unlock 10, lift and close 5 s = 31 s; every step time and the 2 s pack wake is an assumption
check: 31 s against 60 s; step times to measure with riders

claim: With 3 packs charging the cabinet air rises about 4.2 K above ambient
law: Steady heat balance: heat = (wall UA + fan flow x rho cp) x rise = 247 W / 58.4 W/K = 4.23 K, reproduced; it assumes half the fans' free-air flow, a lightly windy outside film and fully mixed air; the independent review finds 8.7 K with the fans off and about 5.5 K in still air, and the air at the packs in closed bays is hotter than the cabinet average
check: 4.2 K in the stated case; still-air and fan-failure cases to add

claim: A pack charges at full rate without passing its 45 C limit at 30 C ambient (R9)
law: Pack temperature = ambient + cabinet air rise + pack rise at the end of constant current; highest ambient for uninterrupted charging 29.4 C (5 % loss bound) to 38.6 C (I2R only); the pack refuses charge above 45 C, so the failure mode is a pause, not damage
check: 29.4 to 38.6 C against the 30 C wanted: the warmest bay may pause just under 30 C; the review notes the figure uses the pack's open-air heat path in a closed bay and a cabinet-temperature start, so the true limit may be lower

claim: An idle cabinet with the fans off stays about 1 K above ambient in the cold
law: Steady heat balance: 30 W of controller load through a wall UA of 28.3 W/K = 1.06 K; the 30 W includes fan power and vent losses through the hood slot and intake are not counted, so the cold-start limit is nearer 0 C than -1 C
check: 1.1 K in the stated case; vent losses to add

claim: A runaway in one bay does not spread to a neighbouring bay for 30 min (R8)
law: Bounding heat soak: 0.85 MJ (0.7 to 1 MJ of the 1.7 MJ stored) into 7 kg of steel liner of c = 490 J/(kg K) is a 248 K rise if all of it stays in the wall; in practice most leaves with the vented gas and ejecta and the gap between liners is air
check: Bound 248 K: propagation is plausible and cannot be excluded on paper; the propagation trial decides

claim: A condensed-aerosol unit stops the flame of a runaway but not the cells (R7)
law: Condensed aerosol interrupts flame chemistry in the enclosed volume and does not cool a cell that makes its own heat and oxidiser; the design keeps a vented path and a steel barrier for the cells themselves (DKH-PRC-001 item 9)
check: Claim restated to flame only; cells are handled by S11

claim: The aerosol stays in the bay long enough to act while the vent path is open (R7)
law: The roof fans ran on alarm and exchanged the plenum air (90 m3/h), sweeping out the agent; fix DKH-DEC-001 D1: on aerosol discharge the fans stop and the plenum is left to the passive hood slot (240 cm2 free area), which vents by buoyancy
check: Retention time to measure in the bay mock-up (TRL 4)

claim: A 30 m/s gust gives a dynamic pressure of about 550 Pa
law: q = 1/2 rho v^2 with rho = 1.225 kg/m3; the 30 m/s gust is the requirement, not a code value for a site (site design wind speed to assess)

claim: The 1,400 x 1,100 x 300 mm concrete pad weighs about 1,109 kg
law: Volume x 2,400 kg/m3

claim: Cabinet, canopy and pad stay upright at a 30 m/s gust (R15)
law: Overturning about the pad's rear edge: 0.9 x restoring moment against 1.5 x overturning moment, factor 1.0 needed (a 6 % margin in wind speed); four M12 wedge anchors at 3.8 kN design tension each, 4.13 kN if the same factors (1.5 on wind, 0.9 on weight) are applied to the anchors; wind from the front only
closed_by: DKH-CAL-001 s11 (7.15 kN m restoring, 3.84 kN m overturning)

claim: The lowest canopy point over the sidewalk is 2.1 m or more above it (R13)
law: Canopy rail height from the model: panel tilted 10 degrees, lowest rail point outside the footprint 2,171 mm

claim: A pack is never charged outside its 0 to 45 C window
law: Lithium-ion cells plate lithium on the anode when charged cold and age fast when charged hot; the SwapCell v0.3 pack reports its window on CAN and the charger contactor opens outside it (SWC-PRC-001 v0.3, SWC-CAL-001)
check: Standard cell behaviour; window enforced by pack and controller

claim: Zinc-coated steel panels, powder coat, stainless anchors and plated fasteners last 10 years on a sidewalk with road salt
law: Zinc corrodes slowly under powder coat; cut edges, rivet holes and the zinc-to-stainless couple at anchors and fixings are the weak points and are sealed or separated by gaskets and washers (DKH-DDR-003); service life is not calculable
check: Coating and fastener life to qualify on a sample cabinet

claim: Aerosol residue after a discharge does not damage the electronics beyond a clean-up
law: Condensed-aerosol residues are fine, slightly conductive and hygroscopic salts; the bay compartments are separate from the technical compartment and the residue is wiped off the bay (DKH-PRC-001 item 9)
check: Residue behaviour to check against the unit's data sheet when bought

claim: A rider lifts a 2.85 kg pack one-handed with no strain
law: Far below the 23 kg load constant of the revised NIOSH lifting equation (NIOSH Publication 94-110, value to confirm; the equation covers two-handed lifts and a one-handed limit is not cited, the margin is a factor of eight); lift height 0.73 to 1.10 m is within the favourable band

claim: Every operable part lies within the 0.38 to 1.22 m reach range (R11)
law: US ADA forward reach range for a seated or standing user, 15 to 48 in; the highest operable part is the pack handle top at 1,105 mm

claim: Fumes of a runaway in a bay do not reach the rider at the front
law: Gas leaves by a plenum to a rear roof hood, away from the street side; the bay door is locked during an alarm (DKH-DDR-002); an enclosed 468 Wh pack makes toxic gas (HF is the usual concern) and the concentration at the door is not calculated
check: Dispersion and a leak path at the door seal to assess

claim: One CAN channel per bay at 250 kbit/s carries the dock traffic at under 3 % load (1.8 % in the script, 2.2 % with worst-case bit stuffing)
law: Frames per second x about 160 bits per worst-case extended frame with stuffing / bit rate

claim: Electronic detection latency is within the 10 s the fire requirement allows (R7)
law: Electronic latency 3.1 s (1 s sample, 2 s confirm, 0.1 s loop); the sensor response comes on top (S26)

claim: The charge contactor opens within the 1 s after detection that R7 allows
law: Decision 0.10 s plus contactor drop-out 0.05 s

claim: Vent gas collecting in the plenum, with the fans stopped by fix D1, does not ignite or explode
law: Unburnt cell gas is flammable and can burn violently after the flame is out; with the fans stopped the passive hood slot (240 cm2) is the only vent, and no explosion-venting area is calculated (raised by the independent review)
check: Gas build-up and venting area to assess; the trade-off against S13 goes to Amish (DKH-DEC-001 O4)

claim: The sensors respond within the remaining 6.9 s
law: Thermal lag of the NTC and detector in the bay air, and smoke entry time, are not in the calculation; vendor data needed
check: To assess when the sensors are chosen

claim: The cabinet reaches IP54 with vent slots, a filtered intake and the roof hood (R9)
law: IP54 is dust-protected and splash-proof; a hood with a rain lip, a gasketed door set and a filtered intake can meet it, but the rating comes from a test, not a calculation
